newsitem.title: SHARJAH: CRICKET-STRANG AND STREAK INSPIRE ZIMBABWE CUP WIN.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-STRANG AND STREAK INSPIRE ZIMBABWE CUP WIN.

text.p: Leg-spinner Paul Strang and paceman Heath Streak inspired a combative display of out-cricket by Zimbabwe which secured a 50-run win over Sri Lanka in the Sharjah Cup on Tuesday.
Defending a modest total of 203 in the 50 overs match, Zimbabwe dismissed Sri Lanka for 153, their last five wickets tumbling for five runs in 17 balls.
Zimbabwe's first victory in the three-nation tournament left them needing to beat Pakistan, who also have only one win, to reach the final.
Sri Lanka, with three victories, have already qualified for Friday's final.
World Cup champions Sri lanka looked well placed at 131 for five in 39 overs, but Zimbabwe raised their game dramatically.

Andrew Whittall removed Ruwan Kalpage and Upal Chandana in one over and Streak, returning for a second spell, dispatched Muttiah Muralitharan and Sanjeev de Silva in seven balls to seal the victory. Streak took two for 12 in 8.1 overs.
Earlier, Strang dealt a double blow in one over, dismissing top scorer Roshan Mahanama, who hit 42 off 70 balls, with five fours, and Arjuna Ranatunga.
Such was Strang's control and economy that the wrist spinner conceded just 16 runs in seven overs, the last three maidens.
Aravinda de Silva, with 32 from 61 balls, kept Sri Lanka's hopes alive, but with the asking rate creeping up every over, he fell to a wild shot against pace bowler Eddo Brandes.
Zimbabwe, batting first after winning the toss, built their total on a 65-run stand for the second wicket between brothers Grant and Andy Flower.
Man-of-the match Guy Whittall, who struck 44 off 55 balls, with two fours and one six, and Alister Campbell put on 66 off 91 balls for the fifth wicket.
